_comment: The skills catalogue policy — the two settings the estate wants on every installed skill, and the recommendation the catalogue makes when a skill deviates. Read by scripts/skills_catalogue.py (`just skills-catalogue` / `--enforce`), referenced from `.w0m/sdlc.json -> skills`. 🔑 Skills are executable instructions loaded into every agent session, which makes them a SUPPLY-CHAIN surface — the phrasing is 1945's own, and this catalogue exists to make that surface enumerable rather than assumed. NOTE the recommended defaults are RECOMMENDATIONS: `just skills-catalogue` reports deviations and exits 0; only `--enforce` blocks. That is deliberate — the user-scope corpus is a developer's own machine, and a gate that fails on it would be unactionable in CI.

recommended._why_managed_project: A project-scope skill is vendored into the repo, declared in the manifest and content-hashed in the lockfile — so a change to it shows up in review and in `w0m skill check`. A user-scope skill (~/.claude/skills) loads into sessions for that developer ONLY, is invisible to the repo, and is invisible to every gate: it cannot be diffed, hashed, or reviewed. Two developers can therefore run the same prompt against different instructions with nothing to detect it.
recommended._why_sandboxed: A skill can ship runnable files, and something else then invokes them by path — Artemio's `just idea-refine-init` did, and broke when upstream swapped the helper's language. `sandboxed: true` asserts that a skill's shipped code is only executed in an isolated environment, never directly on the host. Same meaning w0m-sec already uses: no audited code executes on the host.

defaults._comment: Stack-independent baseline skills recommended across w0m projects (T270). Unlike stack-specific skills, cross-cutting communication and persona skills cannot be inferred from package manifests or file extensions, so entries here carry no `detect` rules.

eli5.reason: Audience-adaptive progressive simplification and self-contained interactive visual HTML architecture explainers (T270).

feynman.reason: First-principles debugging and conceptual gap exposure via the Feynman Technique.

detect_executable._comment: How the catalogue decides a skill SHIPS EXECUTABLE CONTENT — the population for which `sandboxed` is load-bearing rather than decorative. Re-measured 2026-10-26 across all estate surfaces (T508): 6 project:skill pairs qualify (`w0m:mmd-validate`, `w0m:w0m-pixel-clone`, `w0m:webapp-testing`, `w0m:wiki-mode`, `artemio:idea-refine`, `artemio:mmd-validate`). Reported honestly rather than inflated.

overrides._comment: Per-skill exceptions to the recommendation, keyed `<project>:<skill>`. A reason is MANDATORY — an unreasoned override is how a recommendation quietly becomes a rubber stamp.

artemio:idea-refine.reason: Declared false because it IS false, and the catalogue proved it: `just idea-refine-init` in artemio/justfile runs the skill's shipped `scripts/idea-refine.sh` with `bash`, on the host. The inherited `sandboxed: true` default asserted the opposite. The script itself is trivial — it creates `docs/ideas` and echoes JSON — so the exposure is small, but the honest record is `false` plus this reason, not a default nobody chose. ⚠️ Revisit if the skill's shipped code ever does more than mkdir.

w0m:webapp-testing.reason: Ships `scripts/with_server.py`, whose entire job is to start this project's OWN dev servers on real ports, wait for them, run a command against them and clean up. Sandboxing it would defeat its purpose — it exists to exercise this repo on this host. ⚠️ Recorded after READING the file: the first draft of this override named a script that does not exist (`scripts/with-dev-server.sh`), which is precisely the unverified-claim shape this catalogue is meant to expose.

w0m:mmd-validate.reason: Declared false because it IS false: `just mmd-validate` and the pre-commit hook run the skill's shipped `validate.mjs` with `node` on the host. Read 2026-09-30: it only parses diagrams (mermaid over a jsdom DOM shim), with no network call, no child process and no file write. A pen would break the hook for no security gain. Owner direction 2026-10-01: it becomes a portable w0m skills tool for clients (T521). Revisit if its shipped code ever does more than read files.

w0m:w0m-pixel-clone.reason: Ships `scripts/pixel_clone.mjs` and `scripts/test_pixel_clone.mjs` (T132), executed directly with `node` on the host during local pixel-clone token extraction, component emission, and unit testing. Read 2026-10-26: uses stdlib `node:fs` and `node:path` only, with Stage 0 domain allowlisting (`checkAuthorization`), zero network calls, and zero child processes.

w0m:wiki-mode.reason: Ships `scripts/wiki-mode.py` (T128 AC8), a read-only vault methodology inspection and destination-routing helper run on the host via `python3`. Read 2026-10-26: uses Python stdlib only (`argparse`, `json`, `re`, `pathlib`), reads `.vault-meta/mode.json` without writing files, making network calls, or spawning subprocesses.

w0m:security-audit.reason: Ships `validate-findings.cjs` and `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs`, read-only JSON Schema and coverage-ledger validators invoked with `node` on the host during security-audit reporting (`VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md:114`). Read 2026-11-02: uses Node stdlib (`node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:util`) only with bounded input/recursion limits (5 MB, depth 64), zero network calls, zero child processes, and zero file writes.

artemio:mmd-validate.reason: Declared false because it IS false: the client recipe `lint-mmd` runs w0m's canonical `mmd-validate/validate.mjs` with `node` on the host, by an absolute path into the w0m-skills checkout (not the vendored copy). The skill only parses diagrams and writes nothing (read 2026-09-30). The absolute path is a finding for the owner to repair in the client repo, which this policy does not touch (T521 AC8).
